chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ibn Abi ʿUmayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:
Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام was asked about game that was shot in the non-sacred area, then brought into the Haram while it was still alive,
so he said: If he brings it into the Haram while it is alive, then its meat and keeping it become forbidden.
And he said: Do not buy it in the Haram except that which had been slaughtered, and had been slaughtered in the non-sacred area, then brought into the Haram; then there is no harm.

key_terms.إِمْسَاكُهُ: keeping or retaining possession of it
key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: the sacred sanctuary in which special hunting restrictions apply
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: the area outside the sacred boundary of the Haram
key_terms.حَيٌّ: alive at the time it entered the Haram
key_terms.صَيْدٍ: game animal that has been hunted
key_terms.لَحْمُهُ: its meat, meaning its consumption as food
key_terms.مَذْبُوحًا: slaughtered according to valid slaughter before entering the Haram

ai.seo_question: Can hunted game shot outside the Haram be eaten or bought after being brought into the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning hunted game in relation to the sanctuary of the Haram. If game is brought into the Haram alive, its meat and possession become forbidden; however, if it was properly slaughtered in the non-sacred area before being brought into the Haram, then there is no problem in consuming or purchasing it.
